newsitem.title: USA: Haing Ngor murder arraignment postponed.
newsitem.headline: Haing Ngor murder arraignment postponed.

text.p: Arraignment of three suspected gang members for the murder of Oscar-winning Cambodian actor Haing Ngor was delayed on Thursday after one of their lawyers was removed from the case.
Judge James Bascue told Kenneth Kahn he could not continue because he was not on the Los Angeles county bar association's list of lawyers approved to handle death penalty cases.

Kahn represents one of the three accused, Jason Chan, who is charged with murder with special circumstances, meaning he could face the death penalty. Chan is believed by prosecutors to have been the gunman in the Feb. 25 robbery-murder.

Kahn said he would appeal the ruling by the judge, who postponed the formal arraignment of Chan, Indra Lim and Tak Sun Tan until Oct. 30. The three men, alleged members of the "Oriental Lazy Boys" street gang, are charged with felony murder and robbery in the killing of Ngor.

The 55-year-old actor was shot outside his home in the Chinatown section of Los Angeles during what police say was a robbery. Ngor won the best supporting actor Academy Award in 1984 for "The Killing Fields," a movie about the genocidal regime of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia.

Defence lawyers contend Ngor's murder was a political assassination because of the actor's vocal denunciation of the human rights situation in his homeland. In previous hearings, they accused the police of coercing witnesses and manufacturing evidence.
Before Thursday's hearing, Kahn told reporters: "What's happening is they're ignoring the truth because they are on some kind of crazed jihad (holy war) to get these guys."
Assistant District Attorney Craig Hum countered: "One of the nice things about the United States is that anybody can say whatever they want to no matter how stupid it is."
